title: Module Overview: Kⁿ as a K[X]-Module via M
content: Fixing an n×n matrix M turns Kⁿ into a module over K[X], with X acting as M and a polynomial f acting as f(M). Mathlib formalizes this with Module.AEval' M.mulVecLin. This file develops the annihilator theory of that module: the annihilator of the whole space is generated by the minimal polynomial, and for a cyclic vector the annihilator of that single vector is too. This is the module-theoretic core behind the invariant-factor decomposition and the rational canonical form.
mathContext: Kⁿ is a K[X]-module via M; annihilator of Kⁿ = span{minpoly K M}.

title: Matrix vs Endomorphism Minimal Polynomial
content: minpoly_matrix_eq_mulVecLin records minpoly K M = minpoly K M.mulVecLin, bridging the matrix M and its associated linear map. It rewrites M.mulVecLin as Matrix.toLin' M and applies Matrix.minpoly_toLin'. This identification is what lets endomorphism-level Mathlib lemmas (which speak of minpoly of a Module.End) apply to the matrix M.
mathContext: minpoly K M = minpoly K (toLin' M) = minpoly K M.mulVecLin.

title: The Module Annihilator is span{minpoly}
content: kn_module_annihilator_eq_minpoly identifies the K[X]-annihilator of all of Kⁿ (as the AEval' module) with Ideal.span {minpoly K M}. After rewriting to the endomorphism minimal polynomial, it is a direct application of Mathlib's Polynomial.span_minpoly_eq_annihilator. Note K must be passed explicitly (it is an explicit variable in the Mathlib statement). This is the whole-space anchor for the per-vector theory that follows.
mathContext: Module.annihilator K[X] (AEval' M.mulVecLin) = span{minpoly K M}.

title: The Vector-Annihilator Ideal
content: vecAnnIdeal M v is the annihilator of the cyclic K[X]-submodule generated by v — the ideal of polynomials f with f(M)·v = 0. mem_vecAnnIdeal_iff characterizes membership through the AEval' scalar action (Submodule.mem_annihilator_span_singleton). minpoly_mem_vecAnnIdeal shows the minimal polynomial kills every vector (transporting minpoly.aeval through the AEval' equivalence), and minpoly_ideal_le_vecAnnIdeal packages the easy inclusion span{minpoly K M} ≤ vecAnnIdeal M v.
mathContext: vecAnnIdeal M v = {f : f(M)·v = 0}; span{minpoly K M} ≤ vecAnnIdeal M v.

title: Cyclic Vectors
content: IsCyclicVector M v holds when no nonzero polynomial of degree < n annihilates v: aeval M.mulVecLin p v = 0 with deg p < n forces p = 0. Equivalently, v together with its iterates v, Mv, ..., M^{n-1}v spans Kⁿ. Cyclic vectors are exactly those whose order has full degree n, the case in which M is similar to a single companion matrix.
mathContext: v cyclic: ∀ p, deg p < n ∧ p(M)v = 0 ⟹ p = 0.

title: Cyclic Vector ⟹ vecAnnIdeal = span{minpoly}
content: cyclic_vecAnnIdeal_eq_minpoly is the headline: for a cyclic vector with deg(minpoly) = n, the vector-annihilator ideal equals span{minpoly K M}. By antisymmetry, only ≤ needs work. Given f with f(M)·v = 0, reduce 'minpoly ∣ f' to 'f %ₘ minpoly = 0'. Write f = (f %ₘ minpoly) + minpoly · (f /ₘ minpoly); since minpoly(M) = 0 and f(M)·v = 0, the remainder satisfies (f %ₘ minpoly)(M)·v = 0. The remainder has degree < n (natDegree_modByMonic_lt with deg minpoly = n), so IsCyclicVector forces it to zero. Monicity of minpoly — required for the division — comes from integrality of M, witnessed by the characteristic polynomial via Cayley-Hamilton (aeval_self_charpoly).
mathContext: f(M)v = 0 ⟹ (f mod minpoly)(M)v = 0 with deg < n ⟹ f mod minpoly = 0 ⟹ minpoly ∣ f.
